name: Klebelsberg-telep (Hattyas)

sourceChecks.title: Szeged-Klebelsberg-telep története, edited Újvári Edit,2007, ISBN978-963-06-2610-1
sourceChecks.retrieval: Independent full PDF text via public web READ connector; no original PDF byte hash claimed
sourceChecks.interpretationLimit: The source says railway embankment. A current/live rail centerline is not automatically identical to the full embankment. A missing rail-to-water intersection therefore does not refute the source or prove that the physical boundary is absent.

sourceChecks.factualSupport: Municipal city-history article describes Klebelsbergtelep and the Hattyas/Vasutastelep/Klebelsberg historical names, with the1992 restoration of Klebelsberg name. This confirms name identity, not a polygon.

Municipal cycle-network plan mentions a former narrow-gauge railway embankment between Klebelsberg and the Tisza right-bank flood levee. This is a useful historic alignment lead, not explicit authority for the eastern quarter-to-Holtbank closing boundary.
Local association describes cleanup along the former narrow-gauge route, neighboring woods and paths. It supplies place/alignment context but not an exact closed quarter perimeter.

independentGeometryChecks.metricCrs: EPSG:23700, transformed from original WGS84 source coordinates

specificObstacle: Western drain398438047 continues via culvert398438143 to the actual outer waterbank; dyke39429434 supplies a plausible northern corridor. No examined actual current or former rail track intersects the Holtbank: even the closest historic rail is586.030m away, and the eastern industrial spur430272966 is625.628m away. Current mapped rail/embankment evidence therefore does not supply a complete unambiguous east/southeast quarter closure. No line has been invented to bridge it.
possibleRemainingEvidence: Source-era cadastral/rail/quarter plan identifying the complete eastern embankment footprint, including any portion surviving beyond tracks.
An explicit local source that names any connecting eastern/southeastern corridor and its Holtbank endpoint.
A source map with a visible whole-quarter outline that can be manually digitized and independently georegistered.
notClaimed: That no more public source exists.
That the quarter lacks real boundaries.
That a railway track endpoint is necessarily the end of the physical embankment.
That the present water surface necessarily equals the entire historical backwater basin edge.
